title: Forecast says 100, JIT calls say 130
prompt: The forecast delivery schedule shows 100 pieces for the near-term period, but new valid JIT calls require 130. Explain which signal should drive execution, how you check the mismatch, and what you do before changing planning data.
expected_points: Separate horizon-based forecast/JIT delivery schedules from exact short-term JIT execution calls.
Check JIT horizon, latest schedule state, call date/time and customer changes before declaring a conflict.
Use requirements matching to understand whether calls consume, replace, or exceed planned requirements in the configured process.
Protect production/procurement planning from stale schedule interpretation without rewriting valid customer execution demand.
Explain the business impact of under-supplying the valid call versus carrying excess planned demand.
follow_up_questions: What changes if the newest delivery schedule explicitly reduced the requirement before the calls arrived?
Which evidence proves that a forecast is stale rather than the JIT call being duplicated?
red_flags: Says forecast always wins because it came first
Adds 30 pieces manually without reconciling requirements
Treats delivery schedule and JIT call as the same object

title: OEM reuses an external call number
prompt: An OEM sends a new JIT call using an external call number that SAP considers a duplicate. The business says the OEM legally reuses numbers after some time. Build the identity diagnosis without manually renumbering the call.
expected_points: Treat external call number as part of a broader identity context, not as a free text label.
Check customer, sales area, destination or assembly location, uniqueness/reuse rules and the actual message timestamp/context.
Compare the incoming call with the existing call before deciding duplicate versus valid reuse.
Keep message-level identity and business-call identity traceable so retries remain idempotent.
Adjust the owning customer/JIT uniqueness rule or interface mapping only after proving the OEM contract.
follow_up_questions: How would you distinguish an interface retry from a valid reused call number?
What changes if two assembly locations can use the same external number?
red_flags: Looks only at the number and ignores customer/destination context

title: Call control blocks the next action
prompt: A valid sequenced JIT call is received and assigned correctly, but the expected production or delivery action is not allowed. Explain how you investigate call control and status without forcing the call forward.
expected_points: Identify the relevant components group or process generation and current internal/external status.
Check call-control determination and which action is permitted from the current status.
Use the action/status log to find the first failed transition instead of editing the final status.
Separate a valid business call from a configuration or downstream-action failure.
Prove the expected next business state before changing call-control customizing.
follow_up_questions: What if the external customer status moved forward but the internal action failed?
How would you distinguish wrong call-control determination from a failed production action?
red_flags: Lists call-control transactions without explaining the state machine

title: Sequence gaps 101, 102, 105, 108
prompt: JIS calls arrive with sequence numbers 101, 102, 105 and 108. Production wants to stop because 103, 104, 106 and 107 are missing. Explain how you decide whether the gaps are real defects.
expected_points: Do not assume every numeric gap represents missing demand.
Check the raw external sequence, sequence-number profile/check and customer-specific gap rules.
Consider whether other suppliers or component families own the missing sequence numbers.
Verify delivery sequence group and packing-group interpretation before stopping physical execution.
Escalate only when the configured/customer sequence contract shows that a required call is genuinely missing.
follow_up_questions: What evidence would show that 103 belongs to another supplier?
How would the answer change if 105 arrived before 102?
red_flags: Renumbers calls into a continuous sequence

title: One JIS component group is late
prompt: A JIS package has several component groups. One group is late, while the other groups are ready and sequence-correct. Explain how you design the recovery without automatically blocking every ready component.
expected_points: Check customer/package rules to decide whether the late component must hold the whole package or can use subsequent delivery.
Preserve sequence and package references for ready components and the delayed group.
Trace production/stock shortage and replenishment ownership separately from JIT call validity.
Consider planned HU, delivery split and EWM/TM consequences of partial or subsequent delivery.
Keep the customer call lifecycle and completion evidence explicit so partial fulfillment is not mistaken for full completion.
follow_up_questions: What if the customer requires one indivisible handling unit?
How would EWM status affect the ability to change the package after picking started?
red_flags: Cancels the whole JIT call immediately
Ships ready parts without checking sequence/package rules
Treats subsequent delivery as a simple new independent order

title: Customer call changes after supplier forwarding
prompt: Your company is a system supplier. A customer JIS call was already forwarded to an upstream supplier, then the OEM changed or cancelled the original call. Design a safe propagation and reconciliation path.
expected_points: Keep the inbound customer call as the source demand and preserve its relationship to the supplier-facing forwarded call.
Propagate change/cancellation using explicit message and business identity so retries do not create duplicate supplier demand.
Check supplier/component mapping, outbound call status and whether physical supply has already started.
Define compensation or exception handling when upstream execution can no longer be cancelled cleanly.
Reconcile customer call, forwarded supplier call, inbound supply, sequence/package state and final customer delivery.
follow_up_questions: How would you handle an interface retry after the supplier already accepted the cancellation?
What changes if the supplier has already shipped the original sequence?
red_flags: Creates a new independent supplier call with no source reference
Assumes message success proves business cancellation
